Elaine and Bill's amicable separation
After fourteen years of a stormy marriage, Elaine and Bill separate amicably
Separation of Elaine and Bill
After fourteen years of a competitive, open marriage punctuated by betrayals and reconciliations, the couple “separated” (their friends' word), without ever considering divorce; each sank into drink.
Elaine and Bill's public separation
A separation in the eyes of their friends if not of the law; each follows an artist's path. Bill becomes rich and famous, Elaine desperately poor.
Last issue of the Black Mountain Review
The last issue of the Black Mountain Review appears in fall 1957.

The seventh issue (fall 1957) bids farewell to the college, closed that year, and hands over to the Beats: Ginsberg's “America,” an excerpt from Burroughs's Naked Lunch, Rumaker's review of Howl, prose by Kerouac, poetry by Gary Snyder.
North Carolina, then the whole country
Closing of the college
The college closes in 1957, reduced to fewer than half a dozen paying students; a little over a thousand students had spent time there since 1933.
